items.text: Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC, on Nov 19. Xi chaired the session, which ran more than an hour (Breitbart says about 90 minutes). It ended in a four-point 'peace declaration', published in English by Chinese state media. In it the three powers commit to UN reform, to raising production and supply of refined petroleum products and keeping energy flows stable, to stressing state immunity and warning the ICC and similar courts not to overreach, and to a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. The declaration repeats that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Al Jazeera reports that Trump said Xi agreed the Strait of Hormuz must stay open and Iran must not get a nuclear weapon. A separate Trump–Putin meeting earlier in the day centred on Ukraine. Zelenskyy called his exclusion a 'huge mistake' (Epoch Times). Trump left for Washington about an hour after the trilateral ended.
items.notes: Breitbart notes the text was released by Chinese and Russian state media, not by an official US source, so wording of the US version is unconfirmed. No details found on Trump–Xi bilateral trade/chip outcomes (search budget exhausted). CNBC headline also reports pledge to boost oil production and revamp the UN.

items.text: Anthropic (ANT) began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov 19. The first trade, set in Nasdaq's IPO cross at 11:48 a.m. ET, was $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, and the stock touched $114.99. It fell below $100 within about 20 minutes, hit a low of $92.72, and closed at $97.17, up 17.1% on the day, with about 832 million shares traded (Stock Titan). Dario and Daniela Amodei rang the opening bell. In remarks reported by Fox News, Dario Amodei acknowledged the technology's real risks, including misuse and loss of control. The offering raised about $81.3 billion, the largest US IPO on record, and underwriters have until Dec 18 to exercise an option on 147 million more shares.
items.reporter: James Cirrone, Stephen Sorace (Fox); Stock Titan Editorial Team
items.thread: Anthropic IPO and AI market valuations
items.notes: Reuters (via Investing.com) said valuation briefly topped $2 trillion at the open. AP (Stan Choe) confirms the $97.17 close.

items.text: The S&P 500 fell 2% (147.80 points) to 7,175.83 on Nov 19, its sixth straight loss and its longest losing streak in about two and a half years, according to AP. The index is now 8.2% below last month's record. The Dow lost 1,101.11 points (2.2%) to 49,097.06 and the Nasdaq fell 2.3% to 23,879.20, with more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks lower. AP and Reuters cite AI-bubble worries that Anthropic's debut failed to ease, high interest rates, regulatory risk after Democratic midterm gains, and the Nvidia leadership turmoil. Nvidia gave up an early 4.7% gain to close down 3.3%. Reuters notes CME FedWatch puts the odds of a December rate hike at about 94%. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 5.04% as investors sought safety.
items.notes: The Reuters story on Investing.com was written before the close and shows smaller intraday losses (Dow -1.79%, S&P -1.54%). AP's closing figures are used here; Yahoo Finance's closing numbers match AP.

items.text: On Nov 19 the Senate voted 48-51 against a House-adopted concurrent resolution directing Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities with Iran. It was the first war-powers vote since the midterms. Republicans Collins, Murkowski and Paul voted yes. Democrat Fetterman voted no, and Republican Thom Tillis, who had backed an earlier attempt, also voted no, saying the measure would not reach the president and amounted to a statement. CBS notes the vote was largely symbolic because concurrent resolutions are not presented to the president. Stars and Stripes reports Democrats plan to push further resolutions and to use appropriations and defence-funding limits once they take control of Congress in January.
items.reporter: Kaia Hubbard (CBS); Svetlana Shkolnikova (Stars and Stripes)
items.notes: Linked to the Dec 11 funding fight (W-261105-03). The House adopted its version in September, 220-204.

items.text: Late on Nov 18 the Ninth Circuit extended its stay of Judge Edward Chen's order restoring Venezuelan Temporary Protected Status, hours after the Justice Department filed its third emergency application to the Supreme Court. The stay now runs until seven days after the appeals court issues its merits ruling, rather than expiring Nov 20. On Nov 19 Solicitor General D. John Sauer withdrew the Supreme Court application (No. 26A714) in a letter saying the deadline no longer applied, and added that the government would return immediately if the merits ruling went against it. The TPS terminations therefore stay in effect and no work authorisation has been restored. AP reports federal attorneys put about 1,800 Venezuelans in detention and about 330 in deportation proceedings.
items.notes: The SG letter is on the Supreme Court docket. The SCOTUSblog headline was updated to 'withdraws', but the cached body predates the withdrawal. The AP story (Spectrum News) could not be fetched, so the detention figures are relayed second-hand.

items.text: In a Fox News interview aired from China, Trump called the preliminary Iran agreement 'a waste of time', said he wants a lasting deal that would bind a future president, and said the US would 'see what happens after January 1st', without explaining the date. He also said Washington is in contact with Tehran and denied that Vance had been pulled off the Iran talks. A Pentagon official put the war's cost at $48.3 billion as of Nov 13, about 26% above the CBO's $38 billion estimate as of Aug 1 and excluding base damage. On Nov 18 CENTCOM warned that ships taking cargo at sea from vessels loaded in Iran could be treated as blockade violators and face seizure or force. Iran's military claimed three tankers hit mines east of Hormuz, a claim not independently confirmed. Israeli outlet Mako reports Trump is still weighing a joint US–Israel strike, with any decision after his Asia trip.
items.reporter: Gulf News live team (Surabhi Vasundharadevi et al.)
items.notes: A Kerala Kaumudi summary says Trump would assess after 2027. The Fox wording says after January 1. Gulf News mentions a third US carrier group (USS Theodore Roosevelt) arriving in CENTCOM, which CENTCOM calls a scheduled deployment. The mine claim comes from Iran only.

items.text: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security interim final rule on remote access to advanced AI chips was published in the Federal Register on Nov 19 (doc. 2026-23529), after being released on Nov 16. It requires a licence to export or transfer advanced chips to any data centre worldwide that gives companies headquartered in China, Macau or other D:5 countries access to more than 12 million aggregate TPP of computing power. The rule also covers access through intermediaries and requires know-your-customer checks on ownership. It adds licence requirements for advanced-chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, except for US-headquartered users who file monthly reports. It formally rescinds the never-enforced Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. Data centres already serving covered firms have 90 days from the effective date to obtain a licence.
items.outlet: Bureau of Industry and Security / Unite.AI
items.notes: Effective date and comment deadline not verified: the Federal Register page was not reachable (robots-blocked). SCMP coverage notes the impact on Southeast Asian data centres. The rule came days before the Trump–Xi meeting.

items.text: The HHS Office for Civil Rights has finalised changes to the HIPAA Privacy Rule, and the final rule is on Federal Register public inspection (doc. 2026-23429). Covered entities will have 15 calendar days instead of 30 to answer patients' requests for their records, with one extension of up to 30 days. Patients will be able to get records through personal health apps where providers can support it. Free copies will be required more often and fees will need advance notice. Health plans and providers may share information for care coordination, including with social-service and community organisations. The requirement to seek written acknowledgment of privacy notices is dropped. Provisions take effect 60 days after publication, and compliance is due 180 days after that.
items.notes: Announced around Nov 16-17 (Healio dated Nov 17) and not previously logged. The exact Federal Register publication date was not confirmed.

items.text: US District Judge Christopher Cooper heard more than two hours of argument on Nov 19 on the administration's request to dissolve his injunction blocking a two-year closure of the Kennedy Center for renovation. The suit was brought by Rep. Joyce Beatty. DOJ argued the board fixed the procedural defects Cooper identified in May, including through a September revote, and cited safety hazards. The plaintiffs called the review a sham meant to justify a decision already taken. Cooper questioned both sides on the two-year versus four-year renovation options and set no timeline for ruling. His separate order barring renaming the centre for Trump is not at issue.
items.notes: Single trade outlet relaying MS Now. The Kennedy Center Honors move to Capital One Arena on Dec 7.

items.text: Walmart reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $188.8 billion, above the roughly $187.2 billion expected, and adjusted EPS of $0.65 against $0.64 expected. US same-store sales rose 2.9% and e-commerce grew 17%. The company raised its full-year outlook, and CEO John Furner described the results as strong. The retailer's figures are a gauge of US consumer spending going into the holiday season.
items.notes: Only Yahoo's live blog was read. Walmart's own release was not checked.

items.text: JPMorgan Chase said some third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack that may have exposed customer names and email addresses. The bank said its own services were not disrupted. The incident follows a run of high-profile US outages, including the FAA ground stop and the NSANet disruption, though no link has been suggested.
items.notes: Single source, not cross-checked with JPMorgan or wires because the search budget ran out.

items.text: The third round of talks on the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) at the President's Chancellery on the evening of Nov 19 ended in what chief of staff Zbigniew Bogucki called an impasse, and he said the talks are being suspended. PiS, Rozwój Plus, PSL, Polska 2050, Konfederacja, Razem, Konfederacja Korony Polskiej and Demokracja Bezpośrednia took part; KO and the Left again stayed away. According to TVN24 and Interia, Bogucki said all participants agree the TK in its current form must be wound down but disagree on how, including how to end the mandates of sitting judges and of Sejm-elected judges who have not been sworn in. The groups committed to submitting their own proposals next week, with the Chancellery acting as a hub, and Bogucki said the President would accept any agreement reached by those at the table. Interia reports he also called a media leak from the previous round a serious breach of trust.
items.notes: Coverage is consistent across TVN24 (centre-liberal), Interia, Rzeczpospolita (centre-right, very brief) and nczas.info (right-libertarian): all report the impasse in the same terms and none blames a specific party. The '70% agreed' figure from the second round reportedly still stands (Interia). A Goniec piece the same week said a Chancellery TK plan had leaked, but it could not be opened.

items.text: The Sejm accepted 20 of the Senate's 21 amendments to the law banning night-time alcohol sales (22:00–06:00) nationwide and banning alcohol advertising. It rejected only the amendment that would have allowed advertising of 0% beer. Among the amendments kept are a ban on discounts and promotional bundles such as '6+6', exemptions for craft-brewery educational and culinary-tourism events, and, according to nczas.info and Rynek Zdrowia, night-time sales at airports. The law now goes to President Nawrocki and, if signed, takes effect on 1 June 2027 (Rynek Zdrowia). The Left's Joanna Wicha said her club will table further restrictions, including on 'małpki' miniature bottles, alcohol displays at petrol stations, and minimum distances from schools and churches.
items.notes: The Health Committee had recommended rejecting four amendments (0% beer ads, craft beer, airports/free zones, wholesale/liquor-store ads). Only the 0% beer ad was rejected, presumably because rejection needs an absolute majority; no vote counts found. Right-wing nczas.info calls the law authoritarian and urges a veto; TVN24 and Rynek Zdrowia report it neutrally.

items.text: Voting on the Senate's amendments to the law limiting doctors' pay and working time, the Sejm failed to reject the amendment cutting the minimum employment required at a facility from half to a quarter of a full-time post. The vote was 202 for rejection, 198 against and 25 abstentions, short of the absolute majority of 213 needed, so the Senate version stands. According to Alert Medyczny, the Sejm rejected an amendment letting the health minister exempt professions by regulation. It accepted the Senate's removal of provisions allowing doctors to be excluded from NFZ-funded work (the so-called 'lex Cieszyński'). The law now goes to the President.
items.notes: This goes against the Health Committee's Nov 18 recommendation to reject the quarter-time amendment. Only one outlet was read.

items.text: The Sejm passed the government's reimbursement law amendment ('SZNUR') by 417 votes to 0, with 17 abstentions. It creates a National Critical Medicines List and gives a 30% lower patient co-payment for drugs made in Poland from a Polish-made active substance; a Razem proposal for 100% was rejected. It also lets drug programmes be prepared so treatment starts the day reimbursement takes effect, allows simplified reimbursement of imported foreign-language packs during shortages, and lets patient organisations join price negotiations. According to Rynek Zdrowia, most provisions take effect on 1 January 2027, and the bill now goes to the Senate.

The Sejm passed, 403 to 8 with 21 abstentions, the Left-sponsored bill (print 3295) allowing up to 1.5bn zł from the 2026–2027 defence budget to be moved to the Polish Science Fund to co-finance semiconductor production lines. The transfer needs agreement from the defence, finance and higher-education ministers. The money can only be used for chip production capacity, and the Warsaw University of Technology's CEZAMAT centre is cited as ready infrastructure. Deputy Science Minister Marek Gzik said the money would come from savings and planned R&D spending without weakening defence. The bill goes to the Senate.
items.notes: The committees had suspended work on Nov 18 after Defence Ministry objections; the bill came back and passed the next day.

items.text: The Sejm passed the act on fair access to and use of data, 381 to 19 with 33 abstentions, to apply the EU Data Act fully in Poland. Owners of connected devices such as cars and smart appliances will be able to access the data their devices generate and share it with third parties such as repair firms. The President of the electronic communications office (UKE) will supervise, act as data coordinator, take complaints and certify dispute-resolution bodies. Businesses face fines of up to 4% of annual turnover, and fines of up to 100,000 zł apply in other cases, according to PAP.

The Sejm accepted the Senate's amendments to the short-term rental bill (print 2865, amending the hotel services act), which goes to the President. Hosts will have to register in a national register of accommodation facilities and give platforms their ID number. Municipal councils will be able to designate zones where short-term flat rentals are banned, for example to protect monuments, from 1 January 2028. According to Finwire, the Senate amendments concerned the maximum penalties, the state registration fee, the period over which three violations are counted, and penalties for online platforms, but exact figures were not available.
items.notes: This matters for Kraków's housing market. Only one outlet was read.

items.text: The Digital Affairs Ministry said ePUAP was back to full operation on Nov 19, nine days after the security incident detected on Nov 10, and apologised for the long outage. It said every component had passed functional and security tests. Analysis with NASK and the ABW found the attack did not spread to other public systems. Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski has said the attack came from abroad, but no country has been named.

After the 'coalition of the willing' meeting in Berlin hosted by Chancellor Merz, PM Donald Tusk said Donald Trump, on the phone after meeting Xi and Putin, had sounded fairly optimistic, though leaders received this very cautiously. Tusk said Russia has taken no concrete steps despite Putin's statements. He said US envoys Kushner and Witkoff called Poland an exceptional partner and welcomed its place in the five-nation European negotiating group. Citing German government sources, Der Spiegel said the meeting aimed to signal 2027 funding for Ukraine, a just peace taking the current front line as the starting point, and an offer of security guarantees.
items.notes: Summit aims come from Der Spiegel via Polsat. The Polsat piece was still being updated.

items.text: Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka told TVN24 that decisions on measures to stop household electricity bills rising in 2027 may come in early December. He said the government is determined that bills will not rise next year and will act if needed. He said that by then the gas price-freeze bill should be ready to go to the President, and his ministry will have an analysis and prepared options for electricity. He did not say which mechanisms are being considered.

The Defence Ministry scheduled a Distinguished Visitors Day for Nov 20 at the Nowa Dęba training ground for KOALICJA 26.2, the first exercise of the coalition of the willing's Multinational Force – Ukraine (MNF-U). The programme includes a briefing by the MNF-U commander, British General Tom Bateman, and a demonstration of post-ceasefire tasks such as troop movement, equipment repair and training support for Ukraine's army. According to Interia, about 2,800 foreign and 2,000 Polish soldiers from 11 countries take part in the Nov 9–22 exercise, which tests reception, staging and onward movement through Poland. Poland is the host nation and leads logistics, and the ministry says Poland will not send its own troops into Ukraine.
items.notes: Troop totals differ: Interia's headline says nearly 3,000 and its body about 2,800 foreign plus 2,000 Polish; Rzeszów News says about 4,800. No post-event report of the demonstration day was found when this was researched.

items.text: The EU's second Consumer Credit Directive (2023/2225, CCD2) applies from Nov 20, but Poland has not passed an implementing law. The Justice Ministry's new consumer credit bill (UC171) is planned for adoption only in Q2 2027, and the earlier draft UC82 was withdrawn. Legal commentators note that loan contracts in force on Nov 20 generally remain under the old rules until they end, revolving credit being an exception. For now the existing Polish consumer credit act, including the free-credit sanction (SKD), continues to govern Polish contracts.
items.notes: A Dziennik Narodowy headline says the same, but the page could not be opened. No government statement was found. Poland may face Commission infringement action for late transposition, which is an inference, not reported.

items.text: An extraordinary session of Kraków City Council has been called for Wednesday 25 November at 16:00, at the request of the Koalicja Obywatelska and Nowa Lewica clubs, over Mayor Łukasz Gibała's decision to halt metro preparations. Radio Kraków reports that the councillors want the documents and analyses behind the decision, and an explanation of why money planned for documentation and tenders was moved to later years. Głos24 adds that they also want to know what happens to the two running tenders (geological surveys, where bids are already open, and documentation including a feasibility study) and what the city has done to secure funding. Gibała has said the city should not spend millions on preparations without a written government funding guarantee.
items.notes: Radio Kraków page metadata lists Tomasz Hycnar as author while the byline says Ola Sobczak. Głos24 (Marzena Gitler) gives the same date and time.

items.text: Mayor Łukasz Gibała told Gazeta Wyborcza that he wants a local referendum in the first half of 2027, most likely in March or April, with three to five questions. Topics he named are the final shape of the Clean Transport Zone (SCT), limits on short-term rentals such as Airbnb, and whether horse-drawn carriages should stay on the Main Square; KRKnews says small modular nuclear reactors are also being considered. The referendum needs the City Council's consent, and no draft resolution or final question list exists yet. Gibała acknowledged resistance from some lawyers; lawyers have previously cited Supreme Administrative Court case law suggesting the SCT cannot be put to a local referendum. ESKA reports Gibała said he would follow the result even if turnout falls below the 30% validity threshold.
items.notes: Original interview in Gazeta Wyborcza (paywalled, not read). Gazeta Krakowska also covered it (headline mentions nuclear reactors) but its page could not be fetched. The KO-Lewica majority was sceptical of an SCT referendum's legality in October (LoveKraków, 27 Oct).

items.text: At the end of its 18 November session the City Council adopted, by 40 votes with 3 abstentions, a resolution presented by council chair Jakub Kosek on burials that could stir public emotions. According to the KRKnews live blog, it organises existing rules so that people who committed acts of terror or aggression are not commemorated, for example through plaques, monuments or marking of burial sites and dates. Kosek said recent events, a reference to the 7 November Main Square attack, made it especially important. The attacker's body is due to be released to a relative after examinations.
items.notes: Only the KRKnews live blog (22:09 entry) reports this; no resolution text or BIP number found. Exact legal scope unclear.

items.text: Councillors unanimously backed a resolution from council chair Jakub Kosek creating a new city medal, 'Cracoviae Virtus', for people who show exceptional courage in saving others' lives or health. It would sit alongside 'Cracoviae Merenti' and be distinct from the 'Honoris Gratia' badge, which Kosek says is awarded too widely for this purpose. The resolution asks the mayor to prepare the medal concept, with the design proposed to be chosen by open competition. Radio Kraków reported the vote on 19 November.
items.notes: Kosek also proposed public consultations on subsidies for nurseries and children's clubs at the same session (KRKnews).

items.text: The KRKnews live blog reports that after a break the council adopted changes to the 2026 budget for current projects, including urgent repairs. No vote count, amounts or project list were given, and the druk numbers (1622-1626, including the multi-year financial forecast change) were not cited. These amendments were billed as a first step towards closing the roughly 390m zł gap in current spending.
items.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget
items.notes: Whether all druki 1622-1626 (incl. WPF) passed is not confirmed; check the BIP voting record.

items.text: Małopolska police spokeswoman Katarzyna Cisło confirmed to TVN24 that senior constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were shot while stopping the 7 November attacker, wore bulletproof vests they had bought themselves. She said this did not necessarily mean the unit lacked equipment and suggested service vests may not have been issued at the pre-shift briefing; stocks cover about 50% of needs for camouflage vests and about 24% for heavy vests. The vests have been secured as evidence, and police say they will establish how this happened; TVN24 says this includes whether the vests were certified. A police union leader told Radio Kraków both officers are recovering quickly and can now receive visitors.
items.notes: First raised on 12 Nov by Kanał Zero citing the officers' wives. Police say supplies suffice for patrol staff. Health update via o2.pl citing Radio Kraków: https://o2.pl/informacje/dobre-wiesci-z-krakowa-wiadomo-jak-sie-czuja-ranni-policjanci-7352759891507232a

items.text: Former mayor Aleksander Miszalski criticised the halt to metro preparations, arguing it could cost access to multi-billion-zloty EU (2028-2034) and state funding and that the central tram network is near capacity on Basztowa and Karmelicka. He put the cost at 13-15bn zł, with Kraków's share at 8-10%, and noted the budget and forecast had reserved 188m zł for preparations. Senator Monika Piątkowska, a rival in the mayoral race, called the decision bad and short-sighted and urged Gibała to work with the government. Deputy Mayor Wałachowski has said the city would build a metro if outside money appears.
items.notes: Opinion reactions; Miszalski's comments first posted 18 Nov, Piątkowska's reported 19 Nov.

items.text: Deputy Mayor Jan Hoffman told the council that the public hearing on the Music Centre (Centrum Muzyki) agreed that a city company will run the building in 2027, while the long-term management model remains open. KRKnews reports the 2027 operator will be ARMK, described as a transitional arrangement. Hoffman asked KO to fix what he called a flawed draft resolution, and KO's Bartłomiej Kocurek complained that no deputy mayor had joined the earlier discussion.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Relates to W-261106-11 (Mazurkiewicz resolution); the resolution itself was not adopted.

items.text: Kraków's Streetbus for homeless people returns on 1 December and runs until late February 2027, but only in the evenings, KRKnews reports. The morning and afternoon routes were dropped after low use last season (655 and 122 uses versus 5,170 in the evening from January to March 2026). It stops daily at al. 3 Maja by the National Museum (19:30-20:00), TAURON Arena stop 05 on al. Pokoju (20:25-20:50) and Podgórze SKA bus station (21:10-21:40), offering food, hot drinks, clothing and information.

Cyclone Akvan crossed the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast near Gopalpur (about 19.1°N, 84.8°E) between 7:30 and 8:30 IST on Nov 20, according to IMD as reported by Pragativadi and OdishaTV. The storm had weakened overnight from a severe cyclonic storm to a cyclonic storm, and it came ashore with sustained winds of 70–80 km/h gusting to 90 km/h. That is well below the 145 km/h earlier feared for Andhra Pradesh. IMD said the landfall process would continue for about two more hours as the system moved inland. It forecast heavy to very heavy rain over southern and coastal Odisha on Nov 20, easing from Nov 21. Landfall came earlier and further north than the noon forecast for the Narsapur–Puri stretch. By mid-morning no deaths had been reported.
items.outlet: Pragativadi (citing IMD); OdishaTV live blog (Poonam Singh)
items.notes: Damage and casualty figures were not yet available at the time of writing. Earlier IMD forecasts had put landfall between Nellore and Tuni, then between Narsapur and Puri, around noon.

items.text: Ahead of and during Akvan's landfall, Odisha moved more than 3 lakh people to shelters, according to Times Now Navbharat and The Open Press. The Open Press puts the figure at 2,98,676 people in 2,523 relief camps by Thursday evening. Times Now Navbharat reports that about 4,170 pregnant women were moved to health centres and shelters, and that 1,317 of them have given birth. It also counts 418 response teams in the field: 60 ODRAF, 14 NDRF, 216 fire service and 128 tree-cutting teams. Officials flagged 941 villages in six districts as landslide-prone. Railway disruption was heavy, though the counts vary: East Coast Railway figures reported by outlets range from 39 to 47 trains cancelled on Nov 20, with OneIndia Hindi and NPG reporting up to 69 cancelled or rescheduled. Intra-circle mobile roaming was switched on in six coastal districts.
items.notes: Sources differ on train cancellation counts (39, 41, 47, 69 cancelled or rescheduled) and rescue team numbers (418 vs 423).

items.text: In Andhra Pradesh, Srikakulam recorded very heavy rainfall as Akvan approached the coast, and Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts were placed under a red alert, The Pioneer reports. Other northern coastal districts had weather warnings. ETV Bharat says the storm's northward shift towards Gopalpur eased concerns in the state, though IMD still forecast isolated extremely heavy rain in the two northern districts. Stranded Andhra fishermen were being brought ashore on the Ganjam coast with Coast Guard help. As of Nov 20 morning, no rainfall totals, damage or casualty figures for Andhra Pradesh had been published.
items.notes: AP figures on damage and evacuations are pending.

items.text: Jaishankar and Rajnath Singh held the fourth India–Japan 2+2 meeting with Foreign Minister Motegi and Defence Minister Koizumi in Tokyo on Nov 19 (14:40–16:10). The two sides issued a joint statement, according to Japan's foreign ministry. They reaffirmed the 'Special Strategic and Global Partnership' and aligned Japan's FOIP vision with India's IPOI and MAHASAGAR, including through the Quad. They also opposed unilateral changes to the status quo by force or coercion. Japan briefed India on its planned revision of its three security documents. The ministers voiced concern over economic coercion and arbitrary export restrictions without naming China, and discussed the East and South China Seas, North Korea, the Middle East and Ukraine. Rajnath Singh called for early conclusion of the UNICORN-related agreements and a reciprocal ship-repair arrangement, according to ANI.
items.outlet: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan; The Tribune (ANI)
items.notes: Joint statement PDF: https://www.mofa.go.jp/files/101121776.pdf (not read in full). No MEA/PIB text found at time of writing. The next 2+2 is due in India; 2027 marks 75 years of ties.

items.text: According to IntelliNews, a letter of intent at the Tokyo 2+2 opens Indian firing ranges to live-fire training by Japan's Self-Defense Forces, including surface-to-ship missiles. Japan's readout says arrangements for SDF use of an Indian range are to be speeded up, and Arab News Japan reports the aim is to do so within the next year. India is to move its domestic approval of the UNICORN stealth antenna/mast transfer forward. IntelliNews says Tokyo expects India's Acceptance of Necessity by February 2027, under a 'Design with Japan, Make in India' label. DRDO and Japan's ATLA are to begin joint research on missiles and other advanced technology. The two sides also agreed to tabletop exercises between their consular authorities on protecting nationals during overseas conflicts.
items.outlet: IntelliNews (via Yahoo News); Arab News Japan
items.notes: IntelliNews says a letter of intent was signed. Japan's MOFA readout lists no signed documents, only the joint statement. The Feb 2027 AoN date is from IntelliNews alone.

items.text: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi for India's first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, held at Purana Qila on Nov 20–22. Outlook India and Awaz the Voice say he is the first Pakistani federal minister to visit India since May 2023, and the first since the May 2025 military clashes. Pakistani media, citing diplomatic sources, say no meeting with PM Modi is scheduled. Malik is due to speak on Nov 21. Outlook reports that India had invited Pakistan's heritage minister and Islamabad sent Malik instead. The MEA has said there is no change in its Pakistan policy since Pahalgam, after Congress MP Manish Tewari questioned the invitation. India invited 25 countries, and about 15 had confirmed.
items.notes: His name is spelled 'Masood Malik' in some Indian outlets; his full name is Musadik Masood Malik.

items.text: The Sensex rose 989.94 points (1.21%) to 83,021.75 and the Nifty 286.35 points (1.14%) to 25,514.30 on Nov 19, according to Business Today. It was the Nifty's first close above 25,500 since Feb 26. The Nifty Bank hit an intraday record of 63,063 before closing at 62,081.30, up 1.65%. Autos led the gains as metal prices fell, followed by banks (HDFC Bank, ICICI, Axis, SBI) and consumption stocks, while IT remained under pressure. Analysts credited record November foreign inflows and easing crude and metal prices, with Brent near $92. They warned that rate-hike worries could cap gains. BSE market capitalisation rose by about ₹5.53 lakh crore.

Mahanadi Coalfields' ₹8,981-crore IPO, an offer for sale by Coal India, was subscribed 0.39 times overall as of 10:10 IST on day two (Nov 20), according to Groww's tracker. QIBs had bid for 1.26 times their portion, while retail stood at 0.16x, NIIs at 0.09x and employees at 0.06x. Bidding closes on Nov 23.
items.notes: These are intraday figures and will change.

items.text: A teenager, Aryavardhan Singh, son of local BJP leader Onkar (Omkar) Singh, was killed in Gorakhpur on Nov 18 when he was hit by a bulldozer/JCB linked to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow. Outlook reports that police registered an FIR against 66 people, including the operator. CM Yogi Adityanath visited the family, accused the SP of hooliganism and alleged the machine was driven over the boy. He ordered strict action. Akhilesh expressed grief and said party workers would help the family. He accused the BJP of politicising the death and asked supporters to stop using bulldozers at rallies. The SP says the machine was stationary and leaving the venue. The family and BJP workers blocked the Gorakhpur–Deoria road over what they called police inaction, according to Amar Ujala.
items.notes: The boy's age is given as 12 (Deccan Herald headline), 13 (ETV Bharat) or 14 (Outlook, Amar Ujala). ETV Bharat does not mention an FIR. Accounts of how the accident happened are contested between the BJP and SP.

items.text: At a programme in Campierganj, Gorakhpur district, on Nov 19, UP CM Yogi Adityanath said he would file his nomination from Ayodhya in the 2027 Assembly election if SP chief Akhilesh Yadav contested from there, Business Today reports. He was responding to an earlier challenge from Akhilesh. He said the SP chief lacked the courage for a direct contest.

A Supreme Court bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said on Nov 19 that it will take up final hearing of the petitions on the marital rape exception on December 9 or 10. It said it would try to finish before the winter break starting Dec 21. The petitions challenge Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which says sex by a man with his wife, if she is not a minor, is not rape. Senior advocate Indira Jaising appeared for the petitioners.
items.notes: The Deccan Herald link could not be opened (headline only). An earlier option of Dec 2–3 was mentioned in court.

items.text: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan was scheduled to dedicate India's first indigenous inactivated H5N1 avian influenza vaccine for poultry on Nov 20 at ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, which developed it. Telangana Today says it targets the circulating clade 2.3.2.1a strain, for which no specific commercial vaccine had been available. India has recorded more than 500 H5N1/H5N8 outbreaks since 2006, and the outlet says recent infections have also been found in mammals. Reports did not set out a national vaccination policy, including whether vaccination will replace culling.
items.notes: Based on preview reports from the morning of Nov 20. The launch itself is not yet confirmed in coverage.

items.text: Delhi's AQI worsened to 282 ('poor') on the morning of Nov 19, two days after CAQM revoked GRAP Stage III curbs when the daily average had improved to 204, according to an Economic Times report. Nineteen monitoring stations were 'very poor', led by Pusa (361), JNU (356) and Sirifort (354). PM2.5 was the main pollutant. IANS put the morning AQI at 267.
items.outlet: Economic Times (via fvbb aggregator); Social News XYZ (IANS)
items.notes: The GRAP-III revocation on Nov 17 may not have been logged earlier. The two AQI readings differ (267 vs 282) depending on time and source.

items.text: Karnataka Home and IT/BT Minister Priyank Kharge said in a post on X that the state cabinet has decided to seize the book 'Basavamantapa' by Ravi Hanj. He said it vilifies the 12th-century reformer Basavanna and the Lingayat tradition. The report gives no legal basis for the seizure, and no cabinet order was available.
items.notes: Only one source; the cabinet date is not stated. The cabinet also cleared other proposals (Deccan Herald headline; article not accessible).

items.text: Under the second phase of Census 2027, online self-enumeration is open until Nov 30, Amar Ujala reports. Respondents answer a questionnaire of about 40 questions on the portal. UP CM Yogi Adityanath filled in his own form at Gorakhnath Math on Nov 19 and urged residents to take part.

The 57th International Film Festival of India opens in Goa on Nov 20 and runs to Nov 28 under the theme 'Stories Without Borders'. The opening film is 'Fatherland' by Polish director Paweł Pawlikowski, according to ANI and the PIB.
items.notes: Of interest for Poland/Kraków readers because of the Polish opening film.

items.text: Speaking at the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit in New Delhi on Nov 20, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal set out a five-point 'TRUST' agenda for India–US economic ties, IANS reports. The points are: transform supply chains, raise talent through dual degrees and university partnerships, unlock growth beyond the metros, speak candidly about hurdles, and track outcomes. The report did not cover the status of the bilateral trade deal or tariffs.

Trump greeted Vladimir Putin as his 'friend' at their meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and Polish leaders pushed back openly. PM Donald Tusk posted on X 'God, protect us from such friends', then told reporters that Putin is not and will not be Poland's friend. He added that US troops in Poland remain one of the key guarantors of its security and that Warsaw wants close coordination with the Trump administration (rp.pl). FM Radosław Sikorski said the embrace caused 'some unease' and asked whether Trump is more a friend of Putin or of Poland's president. The president's office, through Marcin Przydacz, also said it did not support such gestures, though it stressed that the US negotiates from a position of strength (Defence24).
items.notes: Rare cross-camp criticism: the government and Przydacz (president's office) both disapproved, though Przydacz framed it around US strength. Right-wing Do Rzeczy ran an opinion piece calling Tusk's post 'absurd' (headline only; page failed to load). Sikorski separately called Trump's remark that the war is profitable for the US 'hard-headed but true' (Polsat News). Deputy Defence Minister Sobkowiak-Czarnecka told RMF FM that calling a 'criminal' a friend crosses a line.

items.text: Asked by Fox News reporter Aishah Hasnie on Air Force One about Tusk's displeasure, Trump replied roughly 'well, I can't do anything about it', according to Wirtualna Polska. In the same exchange, WP reports, Trump said Russian drones and 'several small missiles' had landed in Poland 'by mistake'. WP's lead and body attribute the drone remark inconsistently, and no transcript was available to verify it.
items.notes: Based on a Polish translation of a Fox News phone exchange. The drone quote is attributed inconsistently within the WP article and should be checked against the Fox original.

items.text: Tusk attended the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, hosted by Chancellor Merz, where US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner briefed about 30 European leaders and Zelensky after the Shenzhen talks. Tusk had said beforehand that he expected the Americans to share the outcome of the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting. Kushner said afterwards that Russia had agreed to a multilateral format that includes European representatives, and that Trump had approved drafting security guarantees for Ukraine (Kyiv Post). Sikorski warned that peace talks could be used to split the West and said Warsaw would not accept new Russian spheres of influence. Der Spiegel, cited by WP, says about 2,800 multinational troops are training in Poland for a possible post-ceasefire stabilisation mission.
items.notes: Russia's acceptance of a European role is Kushner's claim. On Nov 17, Kremlin aide Ushakov said no agreement on European participation had been reached (Defence24). Poland is part of the European negotiating team agreed in Dublin on Nov 13.

items.text: At the P-TEC ministerial in Warsaw, Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe (PEJ) and the Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium signed a letter of intent to extend their Engineering Development Agreement to further long-lead items for the Lubiatowo-Kopalino AP1000 plant. These include containment-vessel and structural modules. PEJ says procurement has begun for the CA01 containment vessel, made in Japan, and the CA20 module, made in the US, while Polish firms including Mostostal Kraków hold initial orders for CA02/03/05 modules subject to NQA-1 certification. US partners will support PEJ in talks with export credit agencies on financing. No value was disclosed.
items.notes: A letter of intent, not a contract. The first long-lead orders were placed in October 2026. Separately, on the same day the Sejm passed an amendment to the nuclear special act (PAP Biznes digest).

items.text: Orlen and US investment firm Carlyle signed a non-binding memorandum at P-TEC 2026 to build a pipeline of possible energy investments in Poland and the wider CEE region, covering oil, gas, chemicals and fertilisers. Orlen CEO Ireneusz Fąfara and Carlyle's energy chairman Marcel van Poecke signed. State Assets Minister Wojciech Balczun linked it to Orlen's planned Baltic Eagle Gas Hub and said the government set 90 days for next steps. Any transaction is subject to due diligence and regulatory approval, and no value was given.
items.notes: Non-binding. Also at P-TEC: Synthos Green Energy signed with Bulgaria's NEK and Blue Bird Energy on possible BWRX-300 reactors in Bulgaria (not bilateral US–Poland).

items.text: At a P-TEC news conference in Warsaw with Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said he had not heard of any European nation wanting to resume Russian energy imports, Reuters reported. Asked about reports that the US might help Russian gas sales to Europe, including talk of a US investor in Nord Stream, he said he could not confirm them and would not speculate about arrangements after the war. Reuters notes that Orlen signed memoranda on Nov 18 with Slovakia's SPP and Hungary's MVM on possible LNG supply through Polish terminals, with US LNG expected to dominate. No US–Poland government agreement or joint statement was reported from the ministerial day.
items.notes: The Orlen–SPP/MVM memoranda were signed Nov 18 and are not supply contracts. Wojciech Jakóbik notes that re-exporting via Poland must compete with the Greek Vertical Corridor.

items.text: India's Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran said in Mumbai, at the World Federation of Exchanges annual meeting, that the worst of the trade and tariff friction with the US may be over. He tied a settled relationship to India signing a trade deal 'in early December or thereabouts', according to ANI. He cited $11.3 billion in foreign portfolio inflows in the first 18 days of November. His timeline is more optimistic than Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal's Nov 18 statement that signing must wait for a new US tariff framework and the outcome of Section 301 probes.
items.outlet: ANI (via Times of Oman) / Asianet Hindi
items.notes: Conflicting official signals: the CEA points to early December, Agrawal makes signing depend on US tariff architecture, and an unnamed official to PTI (Nov 15) gave March 2027. Nageswaran framed it conditionally ('if').

items.text: Jason Meeks, Deputy Chief of Mission at the US Embassy in New Delhi, told the 23rd India-US Economic Summit (Indo-American Chamber of Commerce) that the two countries are working toward trade that is fair, reciprocal and mutually beneficial. He pointed to cooperation in energy, pharmaceuticals, critical minerals and advanced manufacturing and called the Pax Silica Declaration signed earlier this year historic. He argued for lower trade barriers so US suppliers can reach Indian manufacturers and Indian firms can compete in US markets.
items.notes: He gave no timeline for the deal.

items.text: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi posted a photo of Trump, Xi and Putin seated together in Shenzhen with the comment that 'a compromised PM can never sit at this table'. He claimed an Indian PM would be at such a table under a Congress government. National Herald, which is linked to Congress, reported no response from the government or BJP at the time of writing.
items.notes: The outlet is owned by a Congress-linked company. The X post itself is verifiable but was not opened.
